reason: The named episode (a 1957 trip to Italy to learn plastic-flower production) rests only on popular retellings (a Sri Lankan Daily Mirror feature, a florist's blog, NextShark) and is absent from every reputable source that loads: CK Hutchison's milestones page, the Li Ka Shing Foundation founder page, the Gale business biography, the International Directory of Company Histories entry, Bloomberg via Fortune (2018) and The National. No English founder interview, speech or oral history describing the pivot could be found or loaded (SCMP, NYT, Britannica and Business Standard return 403). The fallback episode, buying the factory site in 1958, has three conflicting motives in the sources (landlord raised the rent; lease could not be renewed; he expected rents to keep rising) and no account in Li's own words, so it cannot meet the 'what he knew at the time' standard. Basic dates also conflict: the company is said to be named Cheung Kong in 1950 (CKH, LKSF) or in 1958 (Gale), and his rise in flowers is put in the 1950s by some and 'around 1960' by IDCH. York Lo's footnoted Industrial History of Hong Kong article (Li's 1958 partnership with the US importer Joseph Markovits Inc.) is the best lead if an editor wants to revisit.
